title: Ukrainian People's Republic
capsule: The Ukrainian State (Українська Держава), commonly called the Hetmanate, was a German- and Austro-Hungarian-backed regime established on 29 April 1918 when Pavlo Skoropadsky, a former Imperial Russian general, was proclaimed Hetman of all Ukraine at a landowners' congress in Kyiv, displacing the socialist Central Rada. Operating under the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk occupation, Skoropadsky ruled autocratically, restored property to large landowners and reinstated much of the old Tsarist administrative order, which made the government broadly unpopular. When Germany collapsed in November 1918 and Skoropadsky pivoted toward federation with the Russian White movement, the Directorate launched an anti-Hetman uprising; he abdicated on 14 December 1918, ending the Ukrainian State and restoring the Ukrainian People's Republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territory claimed by the UNR was never fully controlled and shifted constantly; maps of the period reflect aspirational rather than effective sovereignty, and scholarly reconstructions rely on fragmented military and diplomatic records.
